title: Extend the shared `engram source` reader to describe local changes, so every consumer uses one source_id
outcome: `engram source` reports one source_id object (root commit, submodule HEADs, local changes with Git blob ids), and Engram's launcher consumes it; TermAl and EO switch to it in their own items
acceptance: `engram source --root ABS --json` keeps its existing fields and adds the local delta: for each changed, untracked (non-ignored), deleted or renamed path from the existing root status, its status, rename origin, Git blob id from one non-writing `git hash-object --stdin-paths` call over only the dirty paths (default filters), and mode/type; a deletion is a tombstone without a hash; ignored files are excluded; a clean source reports an empty delta

Each submodule reports its path and actual HEAD from the existing recursive submodule status; dirty or off-pin children report their own delta the same way, clean children need no extra status call, and uninitialized or conflicted children make the result unavailable with a reason

No .git contents are hashed, no repository or index listing is added, and no watcher is consulted; exceeding the existing 1 MiB output or 8 s deadline, or a detected change during capture, makes the result unavailable, never a partial identity
Engram's launcher adapter accepts the extended JSON and records and compares the whole source_id before and after a run, in the same changeset as the reader change

Shared fixtures cover equal and different dirty states at the same commit, additions, deletions, renames, mode changes, ignored exclusion, off-pin, dirty and nested children, overflow and deadline, with expected hashes derived at runtime; existing stored records are unchanged
